diagnoses.description: Date disambiguation failure: the predicted date likely came from a secondary date-like token (or OCR-corrupted label line) rather than the primary header Date field. Dense invoices can contain multiple dd/mm/yyyy strings (header date, print date/time, other metadata), and naive selection (first match / most frequent across OCR variants) can pick the wrong one.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback shows 034.jpg date_correct=false while amount_correct=true. The provided 034.jpg image visibly contains a header block with a labeled Date field near the top (e.g., “Date: 09/03/2018”), while the historical prediction is 2018-08-09, consistent with selecting a different dd/mm token elsewhere or an OCR-mutated DATE→DATA line noted in the run history. This indicates a ranking/selection issue, not OCR absence.

diagnoses.description: Total selection failure driven by OCR digit-flip outlier: the predicted total_amount (702.00) is inconsistent with multiple internal anchors on the receipt (Subtotal/Total incl/Payment/Total Amt Rounded) that agree on a different value. This happens when a single corrupted high-priority keyword line dominates selection or cross-variant voting without an anchor-consistency override.
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback shows 074.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount="702.00". The 074.jpg image shows several summary lines around 102.00 (Subtotal, Total incl. of GST, Total Amt Rounded, Payment), while 702.00 is a classic OCR 1→7 digit flip. The run history also shows the agent’s fallback/voting logic over-trusted a corrupted line/variant. This is a selection robustness issue under OCR noise.

diagnoses.description: Rounding precedence failure: the predicted total_amount likely selected the pre-rounding inclusive total instead of the final payable TOTAL after a rounding adjustment, causing an exact-match miss (often by 0.01).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback shows 077.jpg amount_correct=false while date_correct=true; prediction total_amount="23.26". The 077.jpg image clearly shows “Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26”, then “Rounding Adj: -0.01”, then a bold final “TOTAL: 23.25”. This indicates the pipeline did not enforce a hard precedence rule: final total after rounding wins.

diagnoses.description: Schema/normalization failure: total_amount was emitted as an empty string instead of null. Additionally, this receipt layout includes an “Amount” column header that can trigger split-line fallback to an item amount unless explicitly excluded; OCR may also corrupt the GRAND TOTAL keyword and decimal separator (e.g., 92:80).
diagnoses.evidence: Allowed feedback shows 078.jpg amount_correct=false; prediction total_amount="" violates the task requirement (must be null on failure). The 078.jpg image shows a table header “Description Qty Price Amount” and summary lines “Total: 92.80” / “Grand Total: 92.80” plus payment lines “Cash Received: 100.00”, “Change: 7.20”. The run history shows split-line fallback and keyword/decimal corruption (GrandTota./GrandTotal., 92:80), which can cause wrong selection; regardless, empty string must be converted to null.

quality_impact.rationale: The current candidate image-ocr skill already encodes the key repairs implied by the historical failures: label-tolerant header-date ranking (034), anchor-driven outlier rejection to defeat digit flips (074), hard rounding precedence (077), explicit exclusion of AMOUNT column headers + tight split-line fallback + tolerant GRAND TOTAL matching + decimal-separator normalization + empty-string→null guard (078). Further edits would be largely redundant and risk overfitting; remaining risk is implementation adherence rather than missing skill guidance.

trigger_precision.rationale: Existing guidance is narrowly scoped to receipt OCR and triggers only under specific conditions (e.g., split-line fallback only when keyword line has no digits and is not a header; anchor override only when multiple anchors agree; optional upscaling only as fallback). No additional broadening is needed.

instruction_compliance.rationale: Diagnoses rely only on permitted evidence (field-level correctness feedback, predictions, and provided images/OCR snippets). No oracle values are referenced. No tool execution is requested. No unnecessary skill files are modified.

solution_path_coverage.rationale: Covers all observed failure classes in the run: wrong date among multiple candidates (034), wrong total due to OCR digit flip/outlier (074), wrong total due to rounding precedence (077), and schema/normalization + header-triggered fallback issues (078).

skillaxe_evaluation.overall_rationale: The packet’s evidence indicates the original run’s misses were dominated by receipt-specific selection/normalization under OCR noise, not missing OCR capability. The current candidate image-ocr skill already contains minimal, transferable heuristics to address these failures. The most effective next step is ensuring downstream implementations actually apply the documented rules (especially: anchor-consistency override, rounding precedence, header-line exclusion, and final schema guard), so no SKILL.md changes are proposed in this iteration.

iteration_summary: Diagnosed the four incorrect fields (034 date; 074/077/078 totals) using allowed feedback and the provided images/OCR snippets. No skill file updates proposed because the current candidate image-ocr skill already addresses these failure modes; remaining risk is implementation adherence (applying anchor override, rounding precedence, header exclusion, and final schema guard).
